ORPHAN CAUGHT AND KILLED — a lesson the repo's own detector could not have given me.
I stopped the parity subagent (its work was already committed and independently verified by me, and
it had entered a loop re-arming waits on a pytest run I had earlier killed). Stopping the AGENT
orphaned the pytest run it had spawned: PID 18811 reparented to PPID 1, still burning CPU and still
contending for this worktree against my authoritative run.
scripts/check_orphaned_load.py did NOT flag it, correctly by its own rules — it reports processes
whose accumulated CPU exceeds one hour, and this one was ~16 minutes in. So the detector is a
backstop for long-running leaks, not a substitute for reaping what you spawn.
GENERALISABLE: killing a subagent does NOT reap that subagent's background children. Anything it
started with run_in_background survives it and reparents to PID 1. Check by command line
(pgrep -fl) after stopping an agent, not by trusting the CPU-threshold detector.
Killed with -9; load back to 7.8 with only the properly-parented run remaining.

That subagent also self-reported two instrumentation errors worth keeping: it first lost a result to
output buffered behind 'tail' when its run was killed (exit 144), then armed a wait using 'timeout',
which does NOT exist on this macOS host (GNU coreutils; I hit the same thing earlier in this run) so
it exited instantly instead of waiting. Neither was a test failure. It reported both plainly rather
than papering over them, which is why they are recorded here.
